name: Act of April 11, 1882 ratifying the Crow agreement of June 12, 1880 (cession of the western part of the Crow Reservation)
promises: Royce records that this Act confirmed the Crow agreement of June 12, 1880 for the cession of a portion of their reserve (Royce area 619). The promises of that agreement are recorded under cession-1880-06-12-crow.
landTaken: Royce area 619. The Court of Claims (1935) describes the 1882 cession as approximately 1,559,000 acres.
compensation: The Court of Claims (1935) records the consideration as an annual appropriation of $30,000 for 25 years for the benefit of the Crow (22 Stat. 42).
today: This is the ratification of the same agreement and the same land as cession-1880-06-12-crow, and is counted once there. In 1935 the Court of Claims said there had been no taking of Crow lands, that every cession was made for a consideration, and dismissed the Crow petition (Crow Nation v. United States, 81 Ct. Cl. 238). That was a ruling against the nation.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 906, Act of April 11, 1882, Crow
Crow Nation or Tribe of Indians of Montana v. United States, 81 Ct. Cl. 238 (March 4, 1935)

openQuestions: Same land and event as cession-1880-06-12-crow (Royce area 619): the 1880 agreement and its 1882 ratification. Researched briefly; see that record for the promises.
